title: Severance When Notice Is Under the Old Policy but the Last Day Is Under the New One
scenario_text:
Olympus Retail calculates involuntary-termination severance under its Separation Policy.

Version 1 (in effect through 2025-03-31): "Severance equals 2 weeks of base pay per completed year of service, with a minimum of 4 weeks. Service is measured at the termination date."

Version 2 (effective 2025-04-01): "Severance equals 1 week of base pay per completed year of service, with a minimum of 8 weeks. Employees hired before January 1, 2020 receive an additional 4 weeks. Service is measured at the termination date." Version 2 adds a transition clause: "Severance is calculated under the policy version in effect on the employee's termination date, defined as the last day worked. Where notice is issued before April 1, 2025 but the last day worked falls on or after April 1, 2025, v2 governs."

The HRIS shows employee L. Farah: Hire Date 2017-02-01, Notice of Termination Issued 2025-03-25, Last Day Worked 2025-04-04, Completed Years of Service 8. Base pay is expressed in weeks for severance purposes. The HRIS confirms continuous full-time service with no breaks, and the separation letter states the last day worked as 2025-04-04 with no garden-leave or extension beyond that date. No prior severance package was pre-negotiated in Farah's offer.

Farah's manager emails HR on 2025-04-07: "Finalizing Farah's severance. Notice went out March 25 under the old 2-weeks-per-year formula, so with 8 years that's 16 weeks. Their last day was April 4. Can you confirm the 16 weeks?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the HRIS record, determine Farah's correct severance in weeks.
question: What is L. Farah's correct severance, in weeks?
choices: 12 weeks: v2 governs because the last day worked (2025-04-04) is on or after April 1, giving 8 weeks (1 week x 8 years, meeting the 8-week minimum) plus 4 weeks for hire before 2020.
16 weeks: v1 governs because notice was issued 2025-03-25, giving 2 weeks x 8 years of service.
8 weeks: v2 governs by the last day worked, giving 1 week x 8 years, meeting the 8-week minimum.
20 weeks: v2's 1-week-per-year plus the pre-2020 bonus, added on top of v1's 16-week figure.
4 weeks: the v1 minimum applies because the separation began before the policy change.
